rows.l1_text: From spring, my younger sister was going to attend a new school.
So, my family went to a shop in town to choose a bag.
My younger sister liked blue bags, but my mother said, "Because you'll use it every day, a light and sturdy one is what matters."
My younger sister thought a little and decided on a bag that was blue and light.
On the way home, my younger sister was carrying the bag, looking very happy.
Since ancient times, humankind has refined the art of lodging the life force of plants in fibres.
Dyeing with natural dyes is not a mere chain of chemical operations, but is equivalent to a ritual of dialogue with the material.
First, plants gathered with the changing of the seasons have the pigments hidden deep within them released by heat and water.
However, the extracted liquid is still no more than an unstable colour, and if left as it is, it will fade over time.
Here, an important process called mordanting intervenes.
Through complex formation with metal ions, the colour takes on its true brilliance for the first time and is irreversibly fixed to the fabric.
This series of tasks is the crystallization of advanced technique and aesthetic sense, which sublimates the transient products of nature into lasting beauty by human hands.
From within the fierce torrent of information that is a crime scene, forensic investigators pick up minute traces.
This rests on the absoluteness of biometric authentication, namely that everyone possesses a ridge pattern that is unique for life.
First, at the scene or in the forensic lab, latent fingerprints that cannot be seen with the naked eye are made visible by approaches such as the cyanoacrylate method and optical techniques.
Next, the arrangement of feature points such as bifurcations and ridge endings is analysed precisely.
For the purpose of objective corroboration of the crime, it is only through this meticulous matching work that infallible identification is achieved.
A quiet and logical process for uncovering the truth: that, one could say, is the very essence of fingerprint analysis.
Any disguise can only be rendered powerless before this rigorous scientific verification.
Deep in the darkness where the smell of leather drifts, the moment I drag out the thing that had been in a long sleep, particles of dusty memory fly up.

Those boots, which should be described as crimson, or perhaps as the colour of dried blood, have gone beyond the framework of mere footwear and have become a medium that makes visible the emotions lurking within me.
The texture of the leather that I trace with my fingertips remembers at once the coldness of seasons gone by and the heat that resisted it.
My act of wearing these red shoes is by no means an expedient for keeping out the cold.
It is nothing other than a personal and aesthetic ritual of rebellion that drives a wedge of vivid colour into the landscape of an everyday life homogenized into grey.
When I tie the laces tightly and knock my heels on the floor, the dull sound resonates with the beating of my soul.
Now, shall we not wrap ourselves in this decadent beauty and step out into the cold, unfeeling streets?

In socioeconomic contexts such as global financial markets and supply chains, local decision-making by micro-level agents such as individual companies and investors can never be fully captured by simple linear models.
Rather, in the complex adaptive systems woven by their interactions, nonlinear dynamics via positive and negative feedback bring about unpredictable macro-level order, that is, emergence.
This is precisely because, in the process of countless agents continually adapting on the basis of limited information, unintended innovations and systemic risks suddenly manifest.
It can be said that the true driving force of socioeconomic phenomena resides precisely beyond reductionist analysis, within the emergent properties of the network as a whole.
In recent years, in order to put a stop to the thinning of greenery that accompanies the disorderly expansion of cities, local community garden projects have been emerging in various places.
This initiative is characterized by the point that it goes beyond mere cultivation of plants and simultaneously aims at environmental regeneration and the fostering of social cohesion.

In particular, gardens created through the proactive participation of residents are having a positive effect on nearby green spaces not only in the restoration of biodiversity but also in aspects such as the improvement of the microclimate.
Furthermore, the ripple effects generated by such green hubs are immeasurable.

By organically forming a network with existing green spaces, they complement the function as ecological corridors, and can ultimately become a driving force that raises the environmental literacy of the whole region.
Its social significance is extremely great.
The carbon cycle in the Earth system has maintained a delicate balance on the geological timescale.
However, the rapid human activity since the Industrial Revolution, in particular the mass consumption of fossil fuels and deforestation, has brought serious breakdown to this cycle.
The excess greenhouse gases released into the atmosphere by anthropogenic factors are changing radiative forcing and accelerating climate change on a global scale.
The ecosystem cycles that were once stable have been distorted by the economic activity of modern civilization, and their restoration has reached an extremely difficult phase.
We are being forced, with the survival of civilization at stake, into a fundamental transformation regarding how we should accept this chain of irreversible changes.
Fermentation, a metabolic action of microorganisms, goes beyond the realm of a mere preservation technique and is a chemical art that dramatically expands the potential held by staple foods.
For example, when grains and legumes are eaten as staple foods, the nutrients blocked by their cell walls bear the fate of having low bioavailability.

However, by going through the activity of microorganisms, indigestible components are broken down into low-molecular forms, and not only does nutritional value improve dramatically, but anti-nutritional factors such as phytic acid are also broken down.
Furthermore, amino acids and organic acids intertwine in complex ways, giving staple foods layers of deep flavour and umami.
Grains that were no more than a mere source of energy are elevated into a food culture that fulfils both the sustaining of life and a rich eating experience at the same time.
In that, the indispensable role of fermentation is concentrated.
The history of haute couture goes beyond mere changes in clothing and is the very trajectory of humanity's aesthetic pursuit and technological innovation.
In the Belle Époque period, the delicate embroidery and draping done by the hands of artisans in the atelier were established as an art that envelops the body.
However, in the context of contemporary fashion, this traditional craftsmanship is clashing with, or else fusing with, a new paradigm called digital design.
How are 3D modelling built in virtual space and products generated by algorithms rewriting the pride of the "tailor" of the past?
There, a constant tension between analogue warmth and digital coldness can be seen, and it questions the essence of creativity.
In a tranquil workshop, the maker begins the work from starting a sourdough culture in which wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria live together.

The act of controlling the water temperature and room temperature down to the millimetre and mixing only flour and water goes beyond the realm of mere cooking and also echoes a scientific experiment that nurtures an ecosystem of microorganisms.
The levain, cultured over several days, takes on a distinctive sourness and a rich aroma and forms the framework of the bread.
After that, by going through long, low-temperature fermentation, the gluten network increases in density and undergoes a transformation that also makes it excellent for digestion and absorption.

In the final stage of baking, the dough, having expanded along with high-temperature steam, takes on a golden, hard and brittle crust, and the inside is elevated into a moist yet highly elastic crumb.
This series of steps is an unmistakably artistic creation where the providence of nature and human wisdom intersect.
On an old veranda where the feel of autumn hangs thick, what a small child is turning an innocent gaze upon is a single red fruit held in the palm of the hand.
It was truly an apple clad in a deep crimson, as if the workings of nature and time had been condensed into it.
The child sinks teeth into its skin without hesitation and eats greedily, letting the sweet-and-sour juice run down the lips.
There, there is no room for human designs such as logic or calculation to intervene; there is only a fundamental craving of life and a pure acceptance of the thing before one's eyes.
As sunlight filtering through the trees quietly lights his cheeks, he just silently goes on making his own inner hunger and the bounty of this season into one.
That figure was as if it embodied the very providence of the universe itself.
The small patch of earth set up in a corner of the backyard, that is, the small flower bed, was a miniature of a vast universe for the young child.
Covered in mud, he watches over the sprouting of the plants outdoors every day.
That act goes beyond the realm of mere gardening and resembles a quiet prayer to the laws of nature.
Eventually, in the course of their growth, the plants keep stretching out their stems powerfully, even while at times exposed to harsh weather.
In the eyes of the child who gazes at that sight dwells a sense of awe toward the fundamental toughness that life possesses.
The tiny workings that we adults so often overlook, he keeps recording innocently and solemnly.
Truly, that very attitude of conversing with the earth is surely nothing other than the nurturing of souls who will carry the future.
In the ritual space of a school event, T-shirt design can go beyond mere decoration and function as a manifestation of subtle hierarchies and individuality within the group.

The act of rejecting easy reliance on ready-made products and engaging in dialogue with the material through customization by one's own hands is the essential pleasure of DIY fashion, and is also a reaffirmation of self-efficacy.
When the students put their feelings into the texture of the fibres and spin out their own plot, it is not mere garment-making but is sublimated into the establishment of symbolic self-assertion.
It is this very creative process that transforms the memory of the event into something lasting and sublimates the participants' sense of belonging into something strong.
On the sunlit veranda, a small child is fixing an innocent gaze on a single plant set in a ceramic pot.
In his hand, water drawn into a small vessel.
With a modest gesture akin to reverence, he quietly pours it down onto the surface of the dry soil.
The water is absorbed in an instant into the dark-coloured earth, and will eventually travel into the unseen network of roots.
The quiet process of growth that we adults so often overlook, he is simply watching over with pure affection.
Within the limited universe that is the pot, life, nourished by the blessing that is water, deepens its green as time accumulates.
The child's act goes beyond a mere imitation of everyday activity and is inscribed there as a sublime ritual, akin to a primal prayer for the cycle of life.
It may perhaps be the purest form of dialogue that one without words exchanges with nature.
The endeavour of weaving, with one's own two hands, the miracle of inorganic materials being sublimated into an autonomous entity.
That is precisely the essence of robot making that a beginner confronts in the quiet workshop of their own home.
What one who aspires to the depths of robotics must first embody is nothing other than a gritty process of trial and error rooted in the spirit of DIY.
Through electronics work, one physically implements the "sense organs" and "muscles", such as sensors and actuators.
After that, one builds the "nervous system" that is programming, and strictly synchronizes abstract logic with physical behaviour.
The fusion of logic and physics.
The entire process of this making is truly a lofty intellectual pursuit that draws the principles of the universe in miniature on a desk.

In the liquid medium of wine, terroir functions not as a mere aggregate of meteorological and geological variables, but as a sign system in which geological memory has crystallized within the liquid phase.

A skilled sommelier deciphers the mineral contours and the complex soil-derived aromatic structures unfolding in the glass, and gustatorily reconstructs a territorial context that goes beyond sight and smell.

The accumulation of such sensory knowledge relativizes the old classification systems based on single varieties, sublimates the concept of appellation, which hierarchically positions the individuality of each minute plot, into a more rigorous and dynamic hierarchy, and is redefining the very criteria for evaluating the value of wine, both philosophically and practically.
Companies skilfully use colour theory in branding.
Colour is not mere decoration; from the perspective of semiotics, it functions as a sign that conveys a specific message.
For example, red evokes passion and urgency, and blue evokes trust.
This makes use of unconscious human reactions based on psychology.
Companies deeply understand the symbolic meanings these colours carry and are trying to effectively implant their own identity in the minds of consumers.
In recent years, the theory of parametric design has been becoming an important foundation in the field of urbanism.
This is a method that inputs environmental data such as sunlight and ventilation into an algorithm as variables and automatically generates the optimal block layout.
Rather than relying on the designer's intuition, the aim is to create functional and original urban spaces through calculated logic.
The back of my daughter as she passed through the doors of the new school building, an unknown space, was filled with a faint tension and a curiosity that far exceeded it.
This first day of school in her life does not mean a mere movement from one physical place to another.
It is a departure from an established haven, and an extremely important rite of passage in which she is forced to reconstruct herself within a new social context.
In the miniature society that is the classroom, how will she interact with unknown friends, and how will she fit in?
A time of study under the teacher's instructions, keeping silent yet running the brain at full speed.
Each one of those actions becomes nourishment that fosters her cognitive abilities and sociability.
All that I, as her parent, can do is simply watch over that brave first step quietly, and with a firm prayer.
The attitude of reading architecture not as a mere collection of functions but as a text woven by signs is the core of criticism based on post-structuralism.
This theoretical foundation deconstructs the author's intentions and fixed meanings embedded in a building, and brings to light the social context and contradictions behind them.
As a result, architecture is redefined not as a static object but as an open space whose meaning is constantly renewed by the viewer.
Toward mitigating the global crisis of climate change, curbing emissions in the industrial sector is an unavoidable duty in securing sustainability.

Despite the accelerating introduction of renewable energy, in areas where, due to the nature of manufacturing processes, carbon generation cannot be brought to zero, CCUS plays an extremely important role.

This technology, which does not stop at isolation as mere waste but converts carbon into a resource or else seals it underground, can be the optimal solution at present to the difficult problem of reconciling economic activity and decarbonization.

In order to transcend the environmental limits we face, the social implementation of CCUS will likely further increase its presence as the keystone supporting the transformation of the industrial structure.
For those of us working in busy modern professions, how can the limited lunch time we spend in the office or the study be converted into mental and physical fulfilment?
One answer to that lies in the construction of a sandwich combining peanut butter and jam.
First, prepare good-quality whole wheat bread, and spread peanut butter evenly over its porous surface.
At this point, the scientific backing that the film of fat functions as a barrier preventing the moisture of the jam from soaking in also cannot be ignored.
Next, layer jam, such as raspberry, onto the paired other half, or onto the same slice.

The contrasting harmony that sweetness and saltiness, smoothness and graininess weave in the mouth goes beyond the realm of mere nutritional intake, brings about recovery of cognitive function in a short time, and is completed as an act of eating in which rationality and aesthetics are fused.
The young baker, still in the midst of his training, was silently wrestling with the subtle yet dramatic chemical reactions woven by wild yeast, in an atelier tense with the crisp air before dawn.

In modern commercial baking, uniform efficiency often tends to be given priority, but what he truly craves is the ultimate in the delicate yet complex sourness characteristic of sourdough and the deep savouriness that the grain itself holds.

Taking the subtle elasticity of the dough and the progress of fermentation conveyed through his fingertips as his only compass, he attempts a quiet dialogue with an invisible partner, the microorganisms, by precisely controlling the variables of temperature and humidity.

Going beyond the realm of the mere act of baking bread, there quietly dwelt a sense of reverence for ancient methods and an unshakable resolve as a craftsman to draw out the potential of the ingredients to the limit.
A crisp, bracing cold creeps along the windowpane, trying to freeze the air in the room.
However, the eyes of my young child, standing by the window, were fixed on the yard covered in silver-white, and he was driven by an irrepressible impulse of life.
Paying no mind to the coldness of the harsh winter, he is purely and wholly absorbed in getting ready to play outside.
Though clumsily, he puts his arms through the sleeves of a thick coat, putting on armour to protect himself from the cold air.
In the freezing air, his gesture of fastening the buttons one by one even carried a solemnity like that of a warrior challenging an unknown realm.
Before long, the preparations are complete, and he vigorously pushes the door open.

In his back, as he runs out with innocent curiosity into the outside world where the fierce cold wind strikes his cheeks, was condensed the toughness that human beings inherently possess, which transforms even a harsh environment into enjoyment.
The absolute scarcity and exclusivity that haute couture possesses paradoxically function as a source of trends in the mass market.
The avant-garde forms and lavish use of materials that top maisons present at fashion weeks in Paris and elsewhere, by refusing ordinary consumers direct access, instead arouse an intense craving.
This feeling of longing is eventually cleverly digested by global mass-market brands and sublimated into a price range that anyone can reach.

In other words, it is precisely the exclusive aesthetic that disdains serving only a limited privileged class that plays the role of a compass for trends descending to the ground, and keeps the ecosystem of the modern fashion industry perpetually circulating.

Large-scale asset purchase operations by the central bank, that is, quantitative easing policy, do not stop at the mere supply of liquidity but carry an aspect of distorting the price discovery function in the government bond market.

Under yield curve control, the formation of appropriate risk premiums through market mechanisms is hindered, and as a result, the concern that the price signals of debt, which should safeguard fiscal sustainability, will become dulled cannot be dispelled.

Furthermore, while such unconventional monetary policy can function as an anchor for inflation expectations, we bear the responsibility to recognize coolly that it always carries within it the risk that excess liquidity creates a synergistic effect with upward price pressure in the real economy, culminating in unexpected stagflation or a fiscally led scenario.
In the sustainable development of the technology industry, the presence of venture capital is extremely indispensable.
In particular, their role in handling early-stage startup fundraising does not stop at the mere provision of capital.
By supplying risk money to entrepreneurs who take on highly uncertain technical challenges, they compensate for market failures and nurture the seeds of disruptive innovation.
Furthermore, such funding mechanisms bring a virtuous cycle to the entire ecosystem.

As not only funds but also management know-how and human networks are injected, the growth of individual companies is stimulated, which as a result accelerates social implementation and in turn becomes a powerful driving force that promotes the transformation of the economic structure.
A rock band that loves the local scenery has produced a new original T-shirt.
The one in charge of the design is a member who attends an art university.
What he drew was a graphic of a familiar shopping street.
The reason they deliberately adopted a printing technique with a limited number of colours is to express the nuance of faded memories.
This T-shirt is not mere merchandise but something that gives form to their respect for their roots.
In modern higher education, the uniform knowledge-transmission model can no longer maintain its effectiveness.

In this context, the introduction of adaptive learning platforms, which make possible the presentation of teaching materials optimized to learners' cognitive characteristics through real-time proficiency analysis by artificial intelligence algorithms, is extremely suggestive from the standpoint of pedagogy.
In the field of university education, what is being asked is how faculty will design and operate this system in order to maximize each individual's learning attainment.

In other words, it may be said that its essential educational implication lies in the point that technological innovation does not remain merely a tool for efficiency, but can construct a new epistemological framework that reconciles educational equity and individual optimization.
A startup is founded with an innovative idea as its seed.
In the early stage, it solidifies the foundation of the business through raising funds from investors and aims for rapid growth in the market.

Eventually, when the company matures, the founders and investors choose an exit, that is, an exit strategy, such as acquisition by another company or a stock listing, in order to obtain a return on what they invested.
This is not the end of the business but an important process that signifies a transition to the circulation of capital and new creation.
